channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: Election officials prepare for possible federal interference
item.description: Reuters reporters outline nine scenarios that could strain the 2026 midterms, from seizing ballots to pressuring local officials. More than 50 election administrators and legal experts said courts and established safeguards are likely to hold, but they are preparing for unprecedented disputes.

item.title: EFF warns against federal consolidation of personal data
item.description: EFF argues that combining federal personnel, benefits, immigration and voter records creates errors, invites abuse and chills civic participation. It calls for stronger Privacy Act enforcement, limits on government purchases from data brokers and a comprehensive consumer privacy law.

item.title: Nieman Lab redesigns 18 years of journalism archives
item.description: Nieman Lab rebuilt more than 100,000 URLs with flexible story layouts, refreshed typography, improved search and subscription tools, and new topic archives. Founder Joshua Benton says the cleaner backend replaces years of accumulated PHP and CSS workarounds.

item.title: White House ordered limits on Ukraine's Starshield service
item.description: Reuters reporters Erin Banco and Gram Slattery found that an order to slow the SpaceX military satellite service used by Ukraine came from inside the White House. Ukrainian officials say the restrictions hindered strike missions and drone defenses, exposing the risks of critical systems controlled through one provider.

item.title: W3C makes standards work easier to follow
item.description: New W3C activity pages gather each group's charters, publications, meetings, participants, issues and pull requests into one chronological view. The beta pages replace a scavenger hunt across separate systems and may later add an API plus mailing-list and news data.

item.title: Only half of candidates in key Senate races promise to accept results
item.description: Reuters asked 26 campaigns in 13 competitive Senate races whether their candidates would accept the election outcome. Fourteen gave unconditional assurances; others qualified their answers, deflected or did not respond. The survey measures a basic democratic norm weeks before the midterms.

item.title: Online ads became a channel for large-scale espionage
item.description: Citizen Lab and Confiant say Israeli ad agency Discover-Tech used ordinary-looking ads to track targets and help plant spyware. The ads reached more than 120,000 sites and 75,000 apps, including sensitive government and media networks. Google, Comcast and IAB Europe have removed or suspended the firm. Reuters credits reporter Raphael Satter.

item.title: Gutenberg 24.2 moves collaborative notes into the margin
item.description: Gutenberg 24.2 gives collaborative notes a new home in the content margin, so writers can work without closing the Settings sidebar. It also lets users add categories, tags and posts directly to navigation menus. The release includes more than 60 bug fixes plus accessibility and performance work, as WordPress 7.2 approaches beta.

item.title: Mexico orders digital platforms to shield minors from harmful content
item.description: Mexico will require social networks and streaming services to protect children from violent, sexual and other harmful material, giving companies one month to comply. Officials have met with Meta, Microsoft, Apple, TikTok, Google, X and Huawei. The decree joins a global child-safety push while raising familiar privacy and free-expression questions.

item.title: Judge extends press access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico
item.description: U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly extended an order preserving White House access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico while their lawsuit proceeds. Kelly, appointed by President Trump, said the outlets are likely to show that restrictions imposed after reporting on a ballroom project amounted to unlawful viewpoint discrimination.

item.title: WordPress 7.1.3 fixes seven security flaws
item.description: WordPress 7.1.3 is a maintenance and security release with seven security fixes and four bug fixes. The patched issues include stored cross-site scripting through pending comments, a denial-of-service flaw, second-order SQL injection in WXR exports and disclosure of private or unpublished comments. Site owners are urged to update promptly.

item.title: Podnews weighs new RSS tags against platform lock-in
item.description: Podnews' weekly review examines Libsyn's proposed RSS namespace for ad-slot availability, newsletters as membership and audience-data products, and the expansion of transcripts and person tags. The discussion keeps returning to a foundational concern for podcasting: open infrastructure versus features that pull creators and listeners into platform lock-in.

item.title: Newsrooms build direct audiences beyond big platforms
item.description: The Reuters Institute reports on independent publishers cooperating to extend their reach while rebuilding direct reader relationships. Examples include a human-curated French news portal, Scotland’s community newsroom network and a Paris culture newsletter that grew to 250,000 subscribers before expanding into print and events.

item.title: W3C advances accessibility, open source and web interoperability
item.description: W3C’s September roundup covers an updated WCAG 3.0 draft, a pilot open-source interoperability program, Web Authentication Level 4 and fresh work on digital-rights policy. It also lists newly cross-browser web features and previews TPAC discussions about improving the standards process and its tools.

item.title: European supercomputer bet leans on open-source ROCm
item.description: French cloud company Scaleway plans a Sweden-based supercomputer using AMD Instinct chips and the open-source ROCm software stack. The project is noteworthy for developers because ROCm supports widely used programming tools without tying applications to Nvidia’s proprietary CUDA ecosystem, offering another path around hardware lock-in.
